title: A tagents CLI spec
description: Every verb of a command line program as data. The node CLI, the contract generator and the Rust front door all read the one file this describes.

path.description: The words after the program name that select the verb, e.g. ["sessions", "recent"].

positionals.description: Positionals exactly as the usage text prints them: <ref-json-or-id>, [N], <words…>.

options.description: Option name without the dashes to its kind. The node CLI hands this to util.parseArgs unchanged.

required.description: Option names the verb refuses to run without.

summary.description: i18n key of the one-line summary. The text lives in the language catalogue, not here.

impl.description: Which program serves the verb: the Rust front door or the node CLI. The contract generator and the node CLI ignore it.

effect.description: What running the verb does, for whoever decides whether to let it run: a person reading a permission prompt, or a client sorting tools by their hints. read changes nothing, write changes files, settings or what is on the screen, spawn starts a program or a window that does things of its own (a Claude turn, a Claude session in a window, a command), destructive removes or stops something that cannot be got back, and serve runs until it is stopped, so it is no request/response verb and gets no tool. A verb without one is treated as the least safe kind by everything that reads it. The contract generator reads it; the front door only checks it.

tool.description: false keeps the verb out of the plugin's tools: it stays a CLI verb, in the contract and the references. Absent means the verb is a tool.
